content.content:
body:
        sidebar: @{SidebarScope}

        openFile:
            A file clicked in the @{FileTreeScope} opens in an @{EditorScope},
            in a split beside the chat history: the file on the left taking 50%
            of the width, the chat history on the right taking the rest. The split
            can be resized by dragging its edge. Closing the file closes the
            split.

            When the split opens, it slides in from the sidebar, so it's clear
            where it came from: the file's side grows out of the sidebar's
            edge to its share of the width, the file sliding into view from
            behind that edge as it does, while the chat history gives way
            beside it. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, and
            only then can the split be dragged. A file opened in place of one
            already showing doesn't slide, since the split is already
            open. The @{ChatInputScope} is never split: it stays along the
            bottom, across the full width of prompt mode.

        openDiff:
            A file's @{DiffViewScope}, opened from the @{FileTreeScope}, opens
            in a floating panel over the whole window, the ribbon and sidebar
            included, inset 32 pixels from every edge of the window. The panel
            has rounded corners, a border, and a shadow, and the window behind
            it is dimmed. It leaves the split alone: any file open there stays
            open, unsaved changes and all. Opening another file's diff replaces
            the one in the panel.

            The panel closes with the diff's close button, with Esc, or by
            clicking the dimmed window around it. Opening the file from the
            diff closes the panel and opens the file in the split, as clicking
            it in the @{FileTreeScope} would.

        promptMode:
            The body displays the @{PromptEditor} and any splits, to the
            right of the @{SidebarScope}.

content.text:
Closing a file now animates too. It plays the opening slide in reverse: the editor shrinks back into the sidebar's edge and slides out of view behind it, while the chat history grows back to full width. I haven't watched it in the running app.

- **Width:** it shrinks from whatever width the split had, including one you dragged.
- **Timing:** it takes the same 450ms as opening and settles without bouncing.
- **Reopening:** opening a file while one is still sliding out drops the closing one and slides the new one in straight away.

**Code:** in `src/prompt_mode.rs`, closing a file keeps it on screen long enough to slide out and remembers the pane's last width.

**Test:** the existing open-file test now also closes the file. Over several frames it checks that the pane stays against the sidebar's edge, that it narrows through in-between widths without growing, and that the editor is gone afterwards. The full suite has 122 passing, 1 skipped (it needs the real harness), and the same palette test failing as before. The build has no warnings.

**Spec:** `openFile` in `MainWindow.pi` now describes the closing slide. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass.
